assumptions: Every strategy receives the same candidates, budget, base policy, trainer settings, and paired holdout seeds.
Inline candidate records are synthetic training evidence and their exact emitted bytes are content-addressed.
Successful holdout actions are fixed verifier labels and are not exposed to the selector.

h9_result.claim: Helix has greater paired measured downstream success change than the predeclared random-selection primary baseline.
h9_result.decision_rule: not_supported when the Helix-minus-random paired mean is non-positive; otherwise inconclusive because seed-sensitivity cases are non-independent; other baselines are descriptive
limitations: The categorical reference policy cannot condition its action probabilities on the observation.
Declared diversity and semantic-redundancy groups are synthetic scenario labels.
The holdout evaluates bounded action choices rather than an external repository or production workload.
This is one deterministic local synthetic scenario, not a production estimate.
Seeds are deterministic sensitivity cases and are not claimed to be independent population draws.
Student-t intervals summarize seed sensitivity at small n; they are not multiplicity-adjusted hypothesis tests.
Selection features and expected learning values are input predictions; only paired holdout decisions are reported as measured gain.
Semantic redundancy uses declared scenario groups; the selector itself deduplicates only exact content fingerprints.
Failure-only uses the reference selector's declared secondary ranking behavior when more candidates qualify than fit.

helix_baseline_comparisons.effect_definition: paired difference in measured success change (Helix minus baseline)
